Neha,

We saw a very large spike in p99 tail latency and a noticeable uptick in failed SSE connections between ~19:00-20:10 PST tonight that impacted several of our premium chat rooms. Token generation succeeded for many requests, but clients experienced long stalls (15–30s) and an increase in 500/502 responses on reconnects. Our telemetry shows connection churn and a rise in reconnects per minute.

We attached a short capture of the streaming logs and some client-side traces (streaming-tail-logs-20261102.txt, sysdiag_openchat_1102.zip). Can you confirm whether this looks like a configuration/serving-side throttling or something on your side? This is customer-impacting; our product team is asking for a mitigation plan and ETA.

Impact: several thousand end users intermittently disconnected; revenue-sensitive chat tiers affected.

Thanks — Samir

Immediate actions in flight (we've already escalated to infra):
- Rolling a temporary routing rule to move premium chat traffic to a more conservative serving pool (low-risk fallback) — ETA ~12 minutes.
- Increasing per-connection KV TTL and raising the per-VM concurrent connection soft limit to reduce eviction storms.
- Enabling aggressive reconnect backoff guidance to clients to avoid thundering-herd reconnection pressure.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 19:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Live chat — tonight's 7pm-9pm spike (p99 connections / errors)

Samir / Team — quick triage notes and temporary mitigations we've applied: 

Observation: during the 19:00 window we observed a surge of short-lived websocket/SSE sessions with high early eviction of KV prefixes. This led to repeated cold-kv cache misses and increased per-token latency for affected streams. Contributing factor: a coordinated client reconnect pattern amplified by our connection scheduling, which created backpressure on the dispatcher.

Mitigations applied (applied at ~19:30 PST):
- Increased KV prefix TTL for OpenChat customers by 3x for the affected serving pool.
- Raised per-VM connection soft limit from 6k -> 8k for the pool handling premium rooms.
- Flipped routing to fallback model variant with lower memory pressure for long-lived connections.
- Added a server-side reconnect rate limiter for the next 30m to smooth reconnection bursts.

Preliminary result: p99 for streaming connection latency dropped from ~22s -> ~4.6s within 8 minutes after mitigations. Error rate on reconnects reduced from 1.8% -> 0.3%. We continue to monitor.

Action items next 24h:
- Rishi to open SUP-2147 for a durable fix (better eviction heuristics + connection shedding).
- Runbook update: include a fast rollback path for routing rules and an automated TTL bump for impacted accounts. Link: https://drive.google.com/openchat/night-peak-runbook

Trace ids: 8f3a-11c9 / 8f3a-11d2 (sample).

Marissa

Subject: Executive summary: OpenChat peak-hour streaming surge (actions & ask)

Evelyn — FYI and request for quick approval if needed. Summary of incident and customer impact: 
- Incident window: 2026-11-02 19:00–20:15 PST. Root cause (triage): rapid connection churn + KV eviction creating tail-latency amplification on streaming chat endpoints.
- Customer impacted: OpenChat Labs (premium chat tiers). Estimated affected user sessions: ~12k with intermittent disconnects; ~0.9% revenue impact estimate for the time window.
- Actions taken: temporary routing fallback, KV TTL bump, per-VM connection soft-limit increase, server-side reconnect rate limiting. Observed p99 improvement from ~22s -> ~4–5s and error-rate drop.
- Next steps: SUP-2147 for durable eviction fix; runbook update; recommend outreach to OpenChat to offer a goodwill credit and an engineering sync within 48 hours.

Ask: please confirm we can offer a one-off service credit (est. short-term revenue impact coverage) and approve a post-mortem release to OpenChat tomorrow. If you prefer, I can escalate to finance/partnerships for a formal credit worksheet.

Neha
